{{Quote|You heard of the Tion Hegemony? It's an independent sector located along key hyperspace shipping lanes. Wealthy, powerful and stubborn.|[[Whisper (Cathar)|Whisper]]|<ref name="TOR:OinTH">{{TORcite|type=faction|Republic|Outbreak in the Tion Hegemony|Carrick Station}}</ref>}}
The '''Tion Hegemony''', formally known as the '''Ancient and Honorable Union of the Tion Hegemony''', was an ancient kingdom that spanned during millennia over a large part of the [[Tion Cluster/Legends|Tion Cluster]], in the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim Territories]]. It was reorganized as a [[Sector/Legends|sector]] by the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]] during the [[Imperial Era/Legends|Imperial Era]]. It was also known as the '''Caluula sector''' at that time.

==Astrography==
The original Tion Hegemony encompassed a large part of the [[Greater Tion]], covering the area of the modern Tion Hegemony as well as the surrounding [[Allied Tion sector/Legends|Allied Tion]], [[Indrexu sector/Legends|Indrexu]] and [[Keldrath sector/Legends|Keldrath sectors]].<ref name="Xim Week" /> It was located on the edge of one of [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy's]] spiral arms.<ref name="MtL">''[[Mission to Lianna]]''</ref>

[[File:Tion_Hegemony.jpg|thumb|left|225px|The modern Tion Hegemony and its surrounding [[Sector/Legends|sectors]]]]
The modern Tion Hegemony — during and following the [[Imperial Era/Legends|Imperial Period]] — comprised the northern and eastern parts of the [[Tion Cluster/Legends|Tion Cluster]]. The sector included into two quite different regions: the [[Livien Worlds]] and the [[Back Spiral]]. The first region was a cluster of ancient, averagely-wealthy systems at the head of the [[Desevran Trace]], linking the Hegemony to the [[Perlemian Trade Route/Legends|Perlemian Trade Route]]. It included [[Folende]], [[Livien]] itself, and the sector capital of [[Desevro/Legends|Desevro]]. The region was known as the Livien Worlds for its connection to the ancient [[Livien League]]. The second region, known as the Back Spiral, was a string of systems beyond the [[Indrexu Spiral]] [[Nebula/Legends|nebula]] along the [[Tion Trade Route]]. These worlds were mostly poor and had little to do economically or culturally with the Livien Worlds. The Back Spiral and the Livien Worlds were actually separated by the Indrexu Spiral and even lacked a [[Hyperspace route/Legends|hyperlane]] to connect them directly.<ref name="Xim Week" /> The entire Tion Hegemony contained a total of twenty-seven [[Star system/Legends|star systems]],<ref name="A Guide to the Star Wars Universe">''[[A Guide to the Star Wars Universe]]''</ref> including 175 inhabited planets.<ref name="AOCI:HT" />

==History==
===Ancient history===
{{Quote|In the past, the Tion Hegemony has been aggressive about expanding its sphere of influence. But things have changed.|[[Velnine]]|<ref name="TOR:TinTH">{{TORcite|type=faction|Imperial|Trouble in the Tion Hegemony|Vaiken Spacedock}}</ref>}}
The Tion Hegemony area was one of the most ancient inhabited regions of the galaxy. It had been settled by [[Human/Legends|Humans]] before the creation of the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]] and Hegemony inhabitants had long considered the region as the birthplace of humanity.<ref name="GatORW" />

[[File:Tion_History.jpg|thumb|left|280px|The history of the Tion Cluster]]
The region that would later become the Tion Hegemony had been the heart of [[Xim/Legends|Xim the Despot's]] [[Xim's empire|empire]] tens of thousands of years before the [[Battle of Yavin/Legends|Battle of Yavin]].<ref name="GatORW" /> Two capital planets of Xim's empire — [[Argai]], Xim's homeworld, and [[Desevro/Legends|Desevro]], former capital of the powerful Livien League — were located in the region.<ref name="Xim Week" /> The [[Treasure Vaults of Xim the Despot]] were also built in the Tion Hegemony.<ref name="HSatLL" />

===Old Republic era===
{{Quote|Are you familiar with the Tion Hegemony? An independent sector, they claim to be neutral in the war between the Empire and Republic.|Velnine|<ref name="TOR:TinTH" />}}
The Tion Hegemony state was formed centuries after the fall of Xim's empire. It emerged some time after the numerous feuding states that rose from the ashes of Xim's empire — the [[Honorable Union of Desevro and Tion]], the [[Jaminere Marches]], the [[Indrexu Confederation]] and the [[Keldrath Alignment]] — collapsed after the conquest of the Tion Cluster by the Galactic Republic following the [[Tionese War]].<ref name="Xim Week" /> The Hegemony was established as a monarchy dominated by a nobility<ref name="TOR:OinTH" /> led by the [[House of Tion/Legends|House of Tion]] royal family. The House of Tion administered the region for centuries<ref name="TOR:TMTH">{{TORcite|type=codex|The Modern Tion Hegemony}}</ref> despite intense rivalry with the [[Thirty-seven Families]] from Deservo.<ref name="TOR:KUS" />

In spite of its rich history, the importance of the Tion Hegemony declined in the larger Galactic Republic over the next centuries. Nevertheless, its inhabitants remained proud of their glorious past.<ref name="GatORW" />

[[File:Rakghoul_pandemic.jpg|thumb|left|280px|The [[Tion Hegemony rakghoul outbreak]]]]
At some point during the Old Republic era, the The Hegemony regained independence. During the [[Cold War (Galactic Republic–Sith Empire)|Cold War]] and subsequent [[Galactic War]], both the Galactic Republic and the [[Sith Empire (Post–Great Hyperspace War)|Sith Empire]] negotiated with the House of Tion to obtain the support of the rich Tion Hegemony in the conflict.<ref name="TOR:OinTH" /><ref name="TOR:TinTH" /> Both factions also attempted to influence the [[Livien civil war]].<ref name="TOR:OtT" /><ref name="TOR:QtR">{{TORcite|type=crewskill|Underworld Trading|Quashing the Rebels}}</ref> In [[3639 BBY]],<ref name="TOR_updates">{{TOR_updates|1.1}}</ref> an [[Tion Hegemony rakghoul outbreak|outbreak]] of the [[Rakghoul plague/Legends|Rakghoul plague]] spread across several worlds in the Tion Hegemony.<ref name="TOR:OinTH" /><ref name="TOR:TinTH" /> The infection killed large numbers of civilians and transformed many people into [[rakghoul]]s,<ref name="TOR:KUS" /> which caused the Tion Hegemony to descend into chaos. As four worlds were completely overrun by the rakghouls, the Tion royal family quarantined all worlds in the sector. When the plague was reported on a fifth planet, [[Kaon]], the royal family reluctantly accepted help from the Galactic Republic and the Sith Empire. Republic and Imperial operatives were deployed on Kaon by [[Republic Strategic Information Service|SIS]] [[Chief/Legends|Chief]] [[Rannos]] and [[Darth Nurin]], respectively, in order to fight the rakghouls and help as much survivors as possible. On Kaon, the operatives discovered that the outbreak had been caused by an exiled [[Tionese (group)/Legends|Tionese]] [[Scientist/Legends|scientist]], [[Doctor/Legends|Doctor]] [[Sannus Lorrick]], who was seeking to take revenge on the Tion royal family. Lorrick was later killed during an [[Mission to the Lost Island|assault]] on his [[Lost Island|secret lab]] on [[Ord Mantell/Legends|Ord Mantell]].<ref name="TOR:OinTH" /><ref name="TOR:TinTH" />

Around that same time, an individual was sent to look for valuable artifacts on [[Orma]] and discovered a relic from the height of the Tion Hegemony.<ref name="TOR:TDoH">{{TORcite|type=crewskill|Archaeology|The Detritus of History}}</ref>

===Rise of the Galactic Empire===
In the final years of the Republic, all the bellicose and disparate factions of the Tion Cluster had joined in only two states: the Tion Hegemony and the [[Kingdom of Cron]].<ref name="Xim Week" /> However, the Tion had already lost all of its former glory at that time and was only known as a sad backwater of exhausted, corrupt<ref name="GatORW" /> and poorly administered worlds.<ref name="HSatLL" /> As industry, mineral resources, and cultures declined, the Hegemony subsisted as an agricultural breadbasket for some of the most prosperous Tionese worlds.<ref name="MtL" />

[[File:Felucia_theater.jpg|thumb|right|220px|The [[Felucia theater]] of the [[Outer Rim Sieges/Legends|Outer Rim Sieges]].]]
During the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]], both the Tion Hegemony and the Kingdom of Cron joined the [[Confederacy of Independent Systems/Legends|Separatists]].<ref name="Xim Week" /> In fact, the Separatist cause could be said to have somehow originated in the Tion Hegemony, as [[Count/Legends|Count]] [[Dooku/Legends|Dooku]] broadcast his famous secessionist [[Raxus Address/Legends|address]] from the grim planet of [[Raxus Prime/Legends|Raxus Prime]].<ref name="HNNV53154">{{HoloNetNewsWeb|54|news/1352_1.html|Dooku Spotted in Gree Enclave}}</ref> Moreover, the [[Separatist Senate/Legends|Separatist Parliament]] was established on [[Raxus Secundus/Legends|Raxus Secundus]], in the [[Raxus system/Legends|same star system]].<ref name="TCWEG">''[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars: Episode Guide]]''</ref> The Tion Cluster remained under Separatist control until the end of the war<ref name="TEA" /> and the Hegemony was the scene of numerous battles.<ref name="GBCC" /><ref name="TCWvg" /><ref name="DLTRoDV" />

In retaliation for the allegiance of the two Tionese states to the Separatists, the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]] took control of the Greater Tion after the Clone Wars and divided the region into new sectors. The Tion Hegemony itself was split in four sectors. Its rimward territories became the Indrexu and Keldrath sectors while the heart of the Hegemony was divided in two: the Allied Tion sector and the modern Tion Hegemony. Additionally, the shrunken Tion Hegemony was allowed a nominal independence that was seen as another humiliation.<ref name="Xim Week" /> In any case, the Empire did not consider the Hegemony to be worth enough to ensure direct control of the sector. As a result, the Tion Hegemony became a haven for criminals.<ref name="SWE">''[[Star Wars Encyclopedia]]''</ref>

===Galactic Civil War===
{{Quote|The Tion Hegemony's survey-updating program is running something like a hundred and eighty years behind schedule and getting worse.|[[Han Solo/Legends|Han Solo]]|<ref name="HSatLL" />}}
During the early [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]], the Tion Hegemony became hotbeds of Rebellion. [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebel Alliance]] presence in the Hegemony was discovered by the Empire shortly after the [[Battle of Turkana/Legends|Battle of Turkana]], resulting in a major offensive dubbed [[Operation Strike Fear]].<ref name="XW" />

In [[1 BBY/Legends|1 BBY]], the long lost treasure hoards of Xim were [[Mission to Dellalt|discovered]] on the planet [[Dellalt/Legends|Dellalt]], in the Tion Hegemony, by [[Han Solo/Legends|Han Solo]] and [[Chewbacca/Legends|Chewbacca]].<ref name="HSatLL" />

===Later history===
{{Quote|If they're looking at occupying the rest of the Tion Hegemony, they'd have concentrated their efforts at Lianna. For one thing, it's closer to the Perlemian, which they pretty much control anyway, from Coruscant to the Cron Drift. They've got something else in mind. Maybe using Caluula as a staging area for an attack on Mon Calamari.|Han Solo, about the [[Yuuzhan Vong]]|<ref name="TNJO:TUF" />}}
The Hegemony joined the [[New Republic/Legends|New Republic]] shortly prior [[24 ABY/Legends|24 ABY]] and was represented in the [[New Republic Senate/Legends|New Republic Senate]] by [[Thuv Shinev]].<ref name="AOCI:HT" />

During the [[Yuuzhan Vong War]], the [[Yuuzhan Vong]] were not interested in invading the Tion Hegemony<ref name="TNJO:TUF" /> and only raided the borders of the Tion Cluster.<ref name="Xim Week" /> Near the end of the war, the invaders [[Battle of Caluula|captured Caluula]] in the Tion Hegemony in order to use the planet as a staging area for an [[Defense of Mon Calamari (Yuuzhan Vong War)|attack]] on the [[Galactic Federation of Free Alliances|Galactic Alliance]] stronghold of [[Dac/Legends|Dac]].<ref name="TNJO:TUF" />

==Behind the scenes==
A galaxy map depicting the various destinations of the [[Star Tours/Legends|Star Tours]] travel agency is seen in the queue of the [[Star Tours (real-world)|''Star Tours'']] attraction at [[Disneyland Paris]] and [[Tokyo Disneyland]]. The map erroneously suggests [[Dagobah/Legends|Dagobah]] is in the Tion Hegemony, which is contradicted by many [[Star Wars Legends|Legends]] sources.<ref name="ST">[[Star Tours (real-world)|''Star Tours'']] {{C|Tokyo and Paris only}}</ref>
